research_questions: Which observable support contacts, mass relations, joint chains, and force vectors make a pose physically legible without reducing it to a personality label?
How should static support, controlled imbalance, takeoff, flight, landing, and recovery be routed before pose atoms are sampled?
Which counterbalance and contact-response cues remain visible in a single stylized frame and final crop?
How can pose rules adapt to disability, mobility aids, prostheses, nonhuman anatomy, machines, and supernatural support systems?
Which mechanics are hard compatibility gates and which are creativity-adjustable plausibility relations?
How can evaluation detect broken support or force logic without enforcing one normative human body?

mechanisms.statement: Name the feet, hands, knees, seat, or external surfaces that bear load before choosing a dramatic silhouette.
Relate the projected body mass to the current support region so still poses read as supported and transitional poses show the next contact or momentum cue.
Coordinate ankle, knee, hip, spine, shoulder, and neck changes as a linked response instead of rotating each joint independently.
Show an external force with a visible point of application, direction, and downstream body response rather than a floating impact effect.
Offset an extended limb, heavy prop, or leaning torso with another mass or support change that preserves a plausible whole-body relation.
Keep load-bearing contacts attached to their surfaces and make compression, friction, or deformation consistent with the declared load.
Distinguish static support from takeoff, flight, landing, recovery, or impending loss of balance before applying a static center-of-mass rule.
Describe pose through visible mechanics and task relations, never as proof of personality, morality, gender, diagnosis, or social worth.

candidate_definitions.ubp_support_contact_map: Specify every visible load-bearing body or prop contact and distinguish firm support from incidental touch.
candidate_definitions.ubp_mass_support_relation: Arrange the torso and carried mass so their apparent projection has a plausible relation to the current or next support region.
candidate_definitions.ubp_load_bearing_chain: Identify one continuous joint-and-segment chain that visibly transmits load from the main mass to a support surface.
candidate_definitions.ubp_counterbalance_chain: Pair an extended or loaded mass with a visible compensating mass, joint change, or additional support.
candidate_definitions.ubp_external_force_line: Bind a push, pull, recoil, collision, or carried load to a visible application point, direction, and body response.
candidate_definitions.ubp_contact_response: Show local compression, grip, surface deflection, or frictional alignment where a declared load meets a surface.
candidate_definitions.ubp_motion_phase_router: Route the pose to static support, takeoff, flight, landing, recovery, or controlled imbalance before candidate selection.
candidate_definitions.ubp_joint_range_guard: Reject joint relations that require dislocation, impossible axis reversal, or mutually inconsistent segment orientation unless nonhuman anatomy explicitly permits them.
candidate_definitions.ubp_embodiment_capability_guard: Apply support and joint rules to the declared anatomy, mobility aid, prosthesis, body plan, and locomotion capability rather than assuming an able-bodied biped.
candidate_definitions.ubp_personality_inference_guard: Reject any mapping from posture mechanics to inherent personality, morality, gender, diagnosis, intelligence, class, or worth.
candidate_definitions.ubp_physics_readability_metric: Score whether support, primary load path, force direction, and motion phase remain identifiable in the final crop without explanatory text.

pixel_evidence_definitions.ubp_support_contact_map: The rendered frame visibly identifies each load-bearing contact through overlap, flattening, pressure, or unambiguous surface attachment.
pixel_evidence_definitions.ubp_mass_support_relation: The main body and carried mass visibly align over a current support region or toward a clearly shown next contact in a dynamic transition.
pixel_evidence_definitions.ubp_load_bearing_chain: A continuous sequence of aligned segments connects the principal mass to the primary support without an unexplained break.
pixel_evidence_definitions.ubp_counterbalance_chain: An extended limb, prop, or torso lean is visibly opposed by another mass shift, brace, or support contact.
pixel_evidence_definitions.ubp_external_force_line: The image contains a readable application point and directional body response for the declared push, pull, impact, recoil, or load.
pixel_evidence_definitions.ubp_contact_response: At least one loaded contact shows pressure-dependent grip, compression, deformation, or friction-consistent orientation rather than hovering.

compatibility: Support-contact maps combine with action phases because a landing and a held stance require different support evidence.
Force lines combine with prop affordances when the hand position and tool axis transmit the same load.
Counterbalance chains combine with asymmetric composition without requiring bilateral visual symmetry.
Load-bearing chains combine with costume and hair motion when secondary materials follow rather than contradict the main force.
Embodiment capability guards combine with human, animal, mechanical, prosthetic, aquatic, aerial, and fantastical body plans.
conflicts: A fixed foot combined with a rotating body and no joint or surface response conflicts with contact constraints.
A heavy off-axis prop with no grip, brace, lean, or secondary support conflicts with counterbalance.
A recoil effect pointing one way while hands and torso respond in another conflicts with the external-force line.
Applying quiet-standing support rules to flight or takeoff conflicts with motion-phase routing.
Reading a slouch, spread stance, wheelchair posture, or limb difference as inherent character virtue or defect conflicts with the inference guard.
counterexamples: A dancer in flight can have projected mass outside every current ground support because the image shows an aerial phase.
A deliberately impossible magical levitation pose can omit ground support if the supernatural support mechanism is visibly declared.
A close portrait may not expose enough body to evaluate whole-body balance and should not be failed for missing feet.
A stylized chibi body can use altered proportions while still preserving its own declared contact and joint logic.
A character braced by an off-frame cable may appear unstable unless the crop retains a visible tension cue or the pose candidate is closed.
boundaries: Do not infer internal forces precisely from one stylized image; use the framework as a plausibility grammar, not a biomechanical diagnosis.
Do not require anatomically human joint ranges from nonhuman or mechanical embodiments.
Do not equate visual stability with emotional calm, confidence, dominance, health, or competence.
Do not add balance aids, prostheses, or corrective postures that the user did not request.
Do not sacrifice a declared supernatural rule; instead require a visible alternative support or force explanation when relevant.
domain_limits: The sources study measured human movement and postural assessment, not stylized illustration quality.
The matrix does not calculate true torque, muscle activation, injury risk, or accessibility from pixels.
Underwater, microgravity, aerial, amorphous, and magical motion require domain-specific force models beyond ordinary ground contact.
embodiment_limits: Biped assumptions must be disabled for quadrupeds, serpentine bodies, multiple limbs, wheels, wings, tentacles, exoskeletons, and floating forms.
Joint-range checks must use declared anatomy and assistive or mechanical constraints, not a single normative body template.
Visible body differences and mobility devices are structural facts, never shorthand for fragility, villainy, courage, or dependence.
cultural_limits: Pose mechanics do not establish culturally universal meanings for bowing, kneeling, sitting, pointing feet, or spatial rank.
Ritual and etiquette postures require locale and context rather than being sampled as universal emotional signals.
Body-size, flexibility, age, disability, gender presentation, and dress conventions must not be converted into normative pose scores.
source_biases: OpenSim represents anatomy and forces through model assumptions and is not a direct image-composition study.
The Equimetrix validation emphasizes controlled standing configurations and cannot cover athletic, aerial, aquatic, or fantastical motion.
Both sources privilege measurable human biomechanics and underrepresent diverse embodiments and stylized deformation.
runtime_implications: Store pose atoms outside topic routes and activate them only after embodiment and motion-phase routing.
Select at most one primary support relation and one force or counterbalance relation so mechanics do not crowd out the requested concept.
Close pose slots when the user fixes the pose or crop; never silently replace a declared action with a mechanically easier one.
Require force-bearing props to share contact, axis, handedness, and load metadata with action candidates.
Keep the personality-inference and embodiment-capability guards mandatory at every creativity level.
evaluation_implications: Hold out human, disabled, quadruped, mechanical, aerial, aquatic, and magical embodiments when testing generalization.
Judge support contact, force direction, joint continuity, and phase readability separately rather than with one aesthetic score.
Include negative controls where projected mass lies outside static support but the flight or transition phase is correctly visible.
Check the delivered crop at thumbnail and native scale because feet, grips, and application points may disappear.
Treat physical plausibility as failed only when it contradicts the declared world rule or visible action, not merely real-world normality.

title: OpenSim: a musculoskeletal modeling and simulation framework for in silico investigations and exchange
authority: Peer-reviewed OpenSim framework paper by the platform developers describing bodies, joints, constraints, contacts, and externally applied force vectors.
limitations: OpenSim models movement quantitatively and does not prescribe compelling or readable illustration poses.
Model outputs depend on chosen anatomy, parameters, contacts, and force measurements.
The source does not justify personality or emotion inference from posture.
Stylized, magical, amorphous, aquatic, aerial, and nonhuman bodies require different model assumptions.

title: Equimetrix Device: Criteria Based Validation and Reliability Analysis of the Center of Mass and Base of Support of a Human Postural Assessment System
authority: Peer-reviewed validation study directly measuring center of mass, center of pressure, foot pressure, and base-of-support configurations in human standing.
limitations: The study focuses on controlled human standing rather than rapid action, flight, seated poses, or stylized character art.
Center of mass and pressure are measured variables that cannot be recovered exactly from a single generated image.
The participant and posture range does not establish one normative body or movement standard.
The study provides no evidence for cultural, emotional, moral, or personality meanings of posture.

research_questions: Which visible gesture-form axes can be stored independently of communicative or task function?
How should the runtime represent many-to-many mappings between form and situated function?
Which target, timing, crop, and hand-anatomy evidence is required for a gesture to remain legible in one frame?
How should locale, subculture, era, and audience gate conventional emblems without treating them as universal?
How should occupied, hidden, prosthetic, mechanical, multi-limb, or absent hands close or substitute gesture slots?
Which holdouts distinguish contextually valid variation from random or culturally unsafe hand signs?

mechanisms.statement: Represent handshape, palm orientation, path, body location, and laterality independently from what the gesture is intended to do in the scene.
Assign request, refusal, invitation, indication, emphasis, regulation, depiction, or self-directed action only through a visible target and scene context.
Make pointing and presenting gestures terminate at a visible person, object, region, or explicitly meaningful off-frame direction.
Choose a preparation, expressive stroke, hold, or retraction state whose frozen geometry still communicates the intended action.
Treat conventional emblems as locale- and subculture-scoped mappings rather than universal hand symbols.
Require the selected visible form to be compatible with the situated function without assuming that one form has only one meaning.
Keep the decisive fingers, palm plane, path cue, and target relation readable after crop and overlap.
Never use gesture frequency, size, or form as proof of a person's ethnicity, nationality, gender, diagnosis, intelligence, morality, or personality.

candidate_definitions.ugf_handshape_atom: Specify only the visible digit configuration and degree of hand closure, without assigning meaning by itself.
candidate_definitions.ugf_palm_orientation_atom: Specify the palm plane relative to the actor, viewer, target, and gravity independently from handshape.
candidate_definitions.ugf_motion_path_atom: Specify the implied straight, curved, circular, repeated, expanding, retracting, or halted trajectory using a frozen endpoint and secondary motion evidence.
candidate_definitions.ugf_body_location_atom: Place the gesture relative to face, chest, waist, another body part, shared space, or an external target.
candidate_definitions.ugf_laterality_atom: Declare left, right, bilateral mirrored, bilateral asymmetric, or alternating execution only when the declared anatomy supports it.
candidate_definitions.ugf_target_anchor_atom: Bind the gesture to a visible recipient, object, region, self-contact point, or meaningful off-frame vector.
candidate_definitions.ugf_function_router: Choose a situated function such as indicate, depict, invite, refuse, regulate, emphasize, request, offer, conceal, or self-adjust before selecting visible form.
candidate_definitions.ugf_phase_router: Choose preparation, expressive stroke, hold, or retraction according to which phase remains legible in a still image.
candidate_definitions.ugf_context_binding_guard: Reject a gesture whose claimed function lacks a recipient, target, prior action, dialogue beat, or other visible contextual support.
candidate_definitions.ugf_cultural_emblem_guard: Do not sample a conventional emblem unless the locale or subculture is known and the meaning is explicitly scoped to it.
candidate_definitions.ugf_collision_anatomy_guard: Reject obscured, fused, duplicated, colliding, or anatomically impossible digits and hand paths unless the declared body plan supports them.
candidate_definitions.ugf_gesture_readability_metric: Score whether handshape, palm plane, target, and situated function remain distinguishable in the delivered crop without a caption.

pixel_evidence_definitions.ugf_handshape_atom: The decisive fingers and thumb are individually separable enough to identify the declared open, closed, pinched, hooked, or extended configuration.
pixel_evidence_definitions.ugf_palm_orientation_atom: Foreshortening, thumb side, and wrist relation make the palm plane readable relative to actor and target.
pixel_evidence_definitions.ugf_motion_path_atom: Limb alignment, secondary overlap, cloth or particle response, or repeated elements imply one coherent trajectory ending at the shown hand position.
pixel_evidence_definitions.ugf_body_location_atom: The hand's relation to face, torso, another body part, shared space, or external target remains visible and unambiguous.
pixel_evidence_definitions.ugf_laterality_atom: The image preserves which limb performs each role without unintended mirroring, duplication, or hand swap.
pixel_evidence_definitions.ugf_target_anchor_atom: A line from forearm, hand, or digit direction reaches the declared visible target or exits frame through an intentionally meaningful vector.

compatibility: Form atoms combine across topics because their function is routed from the local scene rather than stored in the handshape.
Target anchors combine with gaze and head direction to create redundant shared-attention evidence.
Gesture phase routing combines with action timing so a hand does not show a retraction while the body shows initial approach.
Culturally scoped emblems combine with explicit locale, relationship, and audience metadata.
Hand silhouette protection combines with prop interaction when grip and communicative gesture are assigned to different hands or phases.
conflicts: Assigning a fixed universal meaning to one handshape conflicts with form-function separation.
A pointing hand with no target or meaningful off-frame direction conflicts with target anchoring.
A hand used simultaneously for a tight grip and an unrelated open-palm gesture conflicts with anatomy and task constraints.
A culturally familiar emblem inserted into an unspecified or incompatible locale conflicts with the emblem guard.
A tiny, back-facing, or fully occluded hand conflicts with claims that fine finger configuration carries the scene's main message.
counterexamples: An open palm may invite, refuse, present, shield, steady, or simply balance depending on target and context.
The same request function may be performed by pointing, reaching, presenting an empty palm, or directing gaze in different scenes.
A beat gesture may emphasize timing without referring to an object and should not be forced into a deictic target class.
A hand inside a pocket can still imply a self-directed adjustment but cannot carry a visible digit-level emblem.
A locale-specific emblem may be valid when the user explicitly requests that cultural context and its meaning is verified.
boundaries: Do not claim that any emblem, palm orientation, finger count, or pointing convention has one meaning across all cultures.
Do not infer intent from hand form alone; bind it to visible context and a declared scene function.
Do not convert sign languages into a loose gesture pool or sample isolated signs without linguistic competence and context.
Do not use offensive, religious, political, gang-associated, or sexual emblems as generic creativity tokens.
Do not diagnose motor ability, neurotype, confidence, honesty, aggression, or status from gesture style.
domain_limits: The sources analyze communicative behavior, not still-image prompting or hand-generation accuracy.
Co-speech timing, sequential repair, and conversational turn management are only partially recoverable in one frame.
Signed languages are full linguistic systems and are outside this generic gesture ontology.
embodiment_limits: Handshape and palm candidates require the declared embodiment to possess compatible digits, joints, and reach.
Nonhuman appendages, prosthetic hands, gloves, tools, and mechanical grippers need capability-specific form atoms rather than forced human fingers.
Laterality must support left, right, bilateral, multi-limb, or absent-hand embodiments without treating one as the default norm.
cultural_limits: Emblems and etiquette gestures must be tagged by locale, community, era, relationship, and audience where known.
A gesture familiar to one language community may be opaque, altered, or offensive in another.
Iconic resemblance can aid interpretation but does not make the resulting function culturally universal.
source_biases: The Visser study analyzes one architectural design meeting and cannot estimate gesture-form frequencies across populations.
The emblem study uses selected Mandarin phrases, learners, native viewers, and curated familiar or unfamiliar gestures.
Both sources concern human communicators and underrepresent disability, sign languages, nonhuman embodiments, and fictional gesture systems.
runtime_implications: Store visible form atoms separately from function routers and cultural mappings.
Select function and target before handshape; creativity may widen form choice but cannot bypass context or culture guards.
Close gesture slots when the user specifies a hand sign, sign-language utterance, occupied hand, hidden hands, or no-gesture pose.
Reserve fine digit-level atoms for crops where hands remain large enough to read.
Log locale and function whenever a conventional emblem is explicitly selected.
evaluation_implications: Use holdouts where the same handshape has different functions and the same function uses different forms.
Test culturally unspecified prompts to ensure no emblem is injected as a universal default.
Score hand anatomy, form readability, target anchoring, and contextual function separately.
Include crops, gloves, occupied hands, prosthetic or mechanical hands, multi-limb bodies, and no-hands cases.
Human review should verify cultural scope for any emblematic mapping rather than judging only visual resemblance.

title: Function and form of gestures in a collaborative design meeting
authority: Primary cognitive-design analysis of naturally occurring gestures that explicitly compares formal characteristics with representational and organizational functions.
limitations: The evidence comes from one architectural design meeting and a restricted set of gesticulations and emblems.
The study does not provide a universal inventory of handshapes or functions.
Dynamic conversational evidence is reduced when adapted to a single illustration frame.
It does not validate image-generation anatomy, pixel readability, or aesthetic quality.

title: Emblem Gestures Improve Perception and Evaluation of Non-native Speech
authority: Peer-reviewed experiments comparing culturally familiar, culturally unfamiliar, and absent emblem gestures in non-native Mandarin speech perception.
limitations: The study tests selected emblems and Mandarin phrases with specific learner and viewer samples, not all cultures or gesture systems.
Viewer judgments in speech perception do not establish universal visual meanings for illustration.
Curated familiar and unfamiliar conditions may not match mixed, diasporic, historical, or subcultural contexts.
The findings must not be used to stereotype gesture use by ethnicity or nationality.

research_questions: Which expressive channels are physically available to the declared species, creature, robot, prosthesis, or hybrid platform?
How can observable channel changes be encoded relative to an individual baseline without claiming emotional truth?
How should attention, warning, readiness, invitation, concealment, and task state be substituted across ears, appendages, surfaces, lights, and actuators?
Which attachment, range, target, and crop evidence keeps a nonhuman signal readable without adding human anatomy?
How should the runtime distinguish communication from locomotion, balance, camouflage, damage, or decoration?
Which cross-embodiment holdouts verify capability gating and prevent anthropomorphic leakage?

mechanisms.statement: Inventory which ears, tails, wings, tentacles, fins, surface cells, lights, panels, joints, or actuators the declared embodiment can actually control before selecting an expression atom.
Describe an observable change from that individual or platform's neutral baseline instead of assigning a human emotion label to a fixed shape.
Allow bilateral or multiple appendages, surface regions, lights, and actuators to change independently when the declared anatomy permits it.

When a human facial or hand cue is unavailable, route its scene function to a capable channel such as orientation, aperture, appendage axis, surface pattern, light animation, or mechanical displacement.
Tie each channel change to a visible attention target, task state, impending action, or interaction beat rather than presenting decoration as a decoded feeling.
For important beats, combine at most two compatible channels that point to the same target or action while avoiding a maximal all-channel display.
Keep the changing organ, appendage, light, or actuator large and separated enough for its baseline difference and direction to survive the crop.
Treat viewer interpretations as hypotheses and never state that ear, tail, wing, tentacle, light, or mechanical configuration proves the being's internal emotion.

candidate_definitions.nxc_channel_capability_router: List the controllable expressive channels supported by the declared species, creature design, prosthesis, machine, or hybrid platform.
candidate_definitions.nxc_neutral_baseline_guard: Require an individual- or design-specific neutral position before interpreting a channel change.
candidate_definitions.nxc_ear_orientation_pair: Specify left and right ear elevation, rotation, flattening, adduction, or asymmetry only for anatomies that support those movements.
candidate_definitions.nxc_appendage_axis_pair: Specify direction, spread, curl, tension, aperture, or asymmetry for a capable tail, wing, fin, tentacle, antenna, or other mobile appendage.
candidate_definitions.nxc_surface_signal_pattern: Specify a visible change in skin pattern, texture, aperture, reflectance, or biological luminescence without assigning a universal feeling.
candidate_definitions.nxc_expressive_light_pattern: Specify light location, color relative to baseline, intensity, rhythm implied in one frame, and the state or action it is meant to expose.
candidate_definitions.nxc_mechanical_state_displacement: Specify an observable panel, lens, antenna, joint, vent, iris, or chassis displacement that the platform can physically produce.
candidate_definitions.nxc_channel_substitution_router: Map attention, readiness, invitation, warning, effort, concealment, or task-state functions to one or two available channels rather than humanizing the anatomy.
candidate_definitions.nxc_context_binding_guard: Reject any channel interpretation that lacks a visible target, task, environmental trigger, interaction partner, or declared platform convention.
candidate_definitions.nxc_emotion_truth_guard: Replace claims of internal emotional truth with observable movement plus a scoped viewer-reading or authorial intention.
candidate_definitions.nxc_channel_readability_metric: Score whether the selected channel, baseline difference, direction, and state or action target remain visible in the delivered crop.

pixel_evidence_definitions.nxc_ear_orientation_pair: Both visible ears have readable bases, tips, and orientations relative to the head, including any declared left-right difference.
pixel_evidence_definitions.nxc_appendage_axis_pair: The chosen appendage has an unbroken attachment, readable axis or curvature, and a distinguishable spread, curl, tension, aperture, or asymmetry.
pixel_evidence_definitions.nxc_surface_signal_pattern: A bounded body region visibly differs from its declared baseline in pattern, texture, reflectance, aperture, or biological light while preserving surface continuity.
pixel_evidence_definitions.nxc_expressive_light_pattern: The emitting element is physically attached to the platform and visibly differs in location, intensity, color relation, or staged sequence cue from its baseline.
pixel_evidence_definitions.nxc_mechanical_state_displacement: A panel, lens, antenna, joint, vent, iris, or chassis element shows a mechanically connected displacement with clear direction and no human-organ substitution.

compatibility: Capability routing combines with any character concept because it runs after the body plan is fixed.
Ear or appendage orientation combines with gaze when both point toward the same attention target.
Expressive light combines with mechanical displacement when one exposes state and the other exposes intended action.
Surface patterns combine with concealment or display actions when the environment and affected body region are visible.
Channel substitution combines with no-face, no-hands, masked, amorphous, robotic, aquatic, aerial, and multi-limb embodiments.
conflicts: Adding human eyebrows, lips, hands, or shoulder anatomy to a nonhuman body solely to express emotion conflicts with capability-based substitution.
Assigning one fixed feeling to flattened ears, a wagging tail, spread wings, curled tentacles, red light, or lowered antenna conflicts with the emotion-truth guard.
A light floating away from any emitter conflicts with platform attachment.
A tentacle, wing, tail, or mechanical panel changing without a coherent attachment conflicts with embodiment continuity.
Activating every available channel at maximum intensity conflicts with readable signal hierarchy.
counterexamples: A species with fixed external ears cannot use ear rotation and should route attention through head, eye, body, light, or another capable channel.
A decorative status light may carry no expressive function unless a platform convention or task context is declared.
A tail position can arise from locomotion or balance rather than communication and should not be decoded automatically.
A cephalopod-like surface pattern may serve camouflage, display, or environmental matching; the picture alone may not reveal internal state.
A machine can communicate clearly through path, stop distance, or tool orientation even when it has no face, light, or anthropomorphic gesture.
boundaries: Do not claim access to a nonhuman animal's or fictional being's subjective emotional truth from visible channels.
Do not force human facial anatomy, hand gestures, biped posture, or gender coding onto a body that lacks those capabilities.
Do not transfer a movement definition from one species, breed, individual, robot, or platform to another without checking morphology and baseline.
Do not assign universal meanings to light color, ear position, tail motion, wing display, skin pattern, or actuator pose.
Do not expose copyrighted AnimalFACS training media or encode protected character-specific signal systems as generic atoms.
domain_limits: The two sources cover domestic-dog facial movement and one mobile robot light interface, not all animals, creatures, or machines.
Tail, wing, fin, tentacle, skin-pattern, and mechanical-displacement candidates are capability-gated design abstractions rather than a universal ethogram.
A still image cannot display true light animation timing or determine subjective state without contextual cues.
embodiment_limits: Every channel requires a declared physical attachment, neutral baseline, movement range, and visibility condition.
Biological and mechanical channels must not be merged into human organs or each other merely for expressive familiarity.
Hybrids may combine channels only when their construction explains how each channel is supported and controlled.
cultural_limits: Viewer readings of animal, monster, mascot, and robot signals are shaped by media convention, culture, experience, and species familiarity.
Light colors and mechanical gestures have no culturally universal emotional dictionary.
Sacred, heraldic, folkloric, or culturally specific creature signals require source-specific context rather than global sampling.
source_biases: DogFACS is anatomy-specific and intentionally avoids interpreting emotion, so it cannot validate generic meanings for other species or appendages.
The expressive-light experiment studies a particular CoBot interface, three animations, and online observers rather than all platforms and cultures.
Both sources favor channels designed or observable by humans and may miss signals outside human sensory ranges.
runtime_implications: Run the capability router after identity and body-plan locking but before expression candidate selection.
Keep human facial and gesture atoms closed when the embodiment lacks those structures; substitute function, never anatomy.
Choose at most one primary and one supporting nonhuman channel for a scene beat.
Store baseline, attachment, controllable range, target, and context metadata with every nonhuman visual atom.
Keep the emotion-truth and context-binding guards mandatory regardless of creativity level.
evaluation_implications: Hold out fixed-ear, floppy-ear, winged, tailed, tentacled, finned, amorphous, robotic, hybrid, masked, and no-face subjects.
Score attachment continuity, baseline difference, direction, target binding, and crop readability separately.
Use adversarial cases where the same channel change is caused by balance, locomotion, camouflage, damage, or decoration rather than communication.
Verify that missing human anatomy stays missing after channel substitution.
Treat viewer interpretations as scoped ratings and never as ground truth about an entity's internal emotion.

title: DogFACS
authority: Official AnimalFACS documentation maintained by the DogFACS development community; defines anatomy-based objective facial movement coding and explicitly disclaims emotion or context inference.
limitations: DogFACS applies to domestic-dog facial anatomy and is not an ethogram or dictionary of emotion.
It does not support universal meanings for tails, wings, tentacles, lights, or mechanical actuators.
Breed and individual morphology can alter which ear or facial movements are possible and visible.
Training videos and test materials have reuse restrictions and are not included in this abstraction.

title: Enhancing human understanding of a mobile robot's state and actions using expressive lights
authority: Carnegie Mellon Robotics Institute publication reporting an online study of animated light patterns used to expose a mobile robot's state and actions.
limitations: The study evaluates one mobile service robot, a light interface, three animations, and nine scenarios.
It supports light as a state-and-action communication modality, not a universal emotion-color code.
Animated sequences lose temporal information when translated into a single still frame.
Results do not validate biological appendages, fictional species, every mechanical platform, or cross-cultural interpretation.
